title: Built an AI stock app that explains why it thinks something's a buy — would this be useful to you?
author: anmenon1204
selftext:
Most investing apps give you a green arrow and expect you to trust it. I got tired of that, so I've been building \*\*Valoryn\*\* — it still gives Buy/Sell/Short signals, but every one comes with the actual reasoning: fundamentals, technicals, news sentiment, institutional activity, in plain English, not just a score.

Screenshot attached of a signal card — curious what people think.

A few things I'd genuinely love feedback on:

	\*\*•\*\*	Would you actually read the "why" behind a signal, or do you just want the arrow?    
	\*\*•\*\*	What would make you \*not\* trust an AI-generated stock call?    
	\*\*•\*\*	Is there anything here that feels like it's missing before you'd try it?

To be clear — this isn't a broker and doesn't execute trades or give financial advice, it's a research/decision-support tool for people who manage their own portfolio. Not launched publicly yet, just trying to figure out if this is solving a real problem before I put more time into it.

Appreciate any honest feedback, including "I wouldn't use this and here's why."

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body: Sorry man, but nobody wants a thing wrapper. Ask yourself whether ChatGPT can do it, there's your answer.

comments.author: Helpful-Capital714
comments.body: Without transparency, this complexity means nothing. I can vibe code stock scoring in like an hour. Show me how it’s accurate and I’ll show you all your flaws.

replies.author: anmenon1204
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback. Can you give me some more details when you say transparency?

replies.author: Helpful-Capital714
replies.body:
Like your weights, calculations, and how the code comes up with the score. The final product looks nice but the calculations are where your code is just guessing. 

You think it’s correct, but we think it’s miscalculated. Now here’s where it gets complicated is even when you ask the AI to show work, it can still just make it look nice. I use 3 layers, research, calculations, and evaluation and you gotta show what happens between each of those stages and then you might be able to have some independent evidence of how it’s calculated.

replies.author: anmenon1204
replies.body: Thank you for the feedback.  I’ll take this into consideration.

replies.author: Helpful-Capital714
replies.body:
Yeah sorry I just don’t know who is actually trying to learn agentic engineering and who is just trying to showboat their latest vibe coding project. If you want a real starting place, try this website from my professor. He teaches the class on agentic engineering.

https://davisjam.github.io/model-based-agentic-software-engineering/teach/

replies.author: anmenon1204
replies.body:
Appreciate the link, I’ll check it out for sure and fair skepticism — talk is cheap on this stuff.

Closing the loop on what I said I'd look at: the score is no longer something the model invents. I separated it into an actual calculation stage — a weighted formula on real inputs (PE valuation band, distance from the 52-week high, distance from the 50-day moving average), computed in code from live market data. The model's job now is narrower: explain a score it didn't get to make up, not generate the number itself. That was a genuine gap you caught, not a nitpick.

Not launched yet, but wanted to actually show the fix rather than just say "noted." Will drop back in here when it's live if folks want to see where it landed.

comments.author: Drakula106
comments.body:
To be clear – ….. you’re about to learn that vibe coding some shit is easy. Distribution and making something useful for people is hard.

You’re better off building something that you can use to trade with and consistently profit. Then people might care.

comments.author: regnull
comments.body: I don’t understand all the negativity. Good job. Yes, stuff is harder than it looks, I started my vibe app 15 months ago, now 1600+ PRs in, lol. It’s important to start. Keep it up!
